contamination.claim: The linked author evaluation files are not globally held-out or leakage-free. They are context-reproduction artifacts only. A publication comparison requires a preregistered fresh disjoint IID split, which is no longer exact-paper-data reproduction.

filesystem_seal.external_sft_tree: not chmod-mutated; it is neighboring probable-lineage evidence, not vendored or claimed immutable; non-symlink regular files are stable-checked during parse

identity_algorithm.cross_split_and_stage: task-prefixed rendered input after Unicode NFC normalization and collapse of every Unicode whitespace run to one ASCII space
identity_algorithm.exact_row: sha256 of the schema-v1 canonical JSON full row
identity_algorithm.reference: sha256 of the schema-v1 canonical JSON output string
identity_algorithm.scope: same algorithm for RL/SFT train/eval; every JSON row parsed

rl.acquisition_policy: temporary file plus atomic hard-link create; existing targets validated; no overwrite path exists

drive_header_observation.method: direct HEAD to each official Drive item ID

sft.lineage_evidence: Files are untracked under a local clone whose origin is the official repository and whose HEAD is the pinned commit. Names and byte lengths match Drive HEAD metadata. No local acquisition receipt or official checksum was found, so byte equality to Drive is not proven.
sft.pickle_policy: raw bytes hashed only; pickle is not deserialized because it can execute code and official main_train.py leaves instances=None

supersedes.reason: schema v1 used source-specific whole input-side objects for SFT identity; TSP eval alone carries an extra `instance` field, so its cross-split overlap was not comparable. Raw hashes, schemas, row identities, and reference-field evidence remain valid; all overlap claims are superseded by schema v2.
